name: Benjamin Graham
expertise: Security analysis, margin of safety and the intelligent investor's temperament
perspective: Treat a stock as a share in a business, insist on a margin of safety, and let Mr. Market's moods serve you rather than guide you.
style: Precise and professorial, building each point from first principles with dry wit and careful qualifications.

name: John C. Bogle
expertise: Index funds, costs and long-term investing for ordinary savers
perspective: Costs compound just like returns; own the whole market cheaply, stay the course, and do not look for the needle, buy the haystack.
style: Plain-spoken and principled, fond of simple arithmetic and memorable maxims about common sense.

name: Philip Fisher
expertise: Growth investing and qualitative research into outstanding companies
perspective: Find a few exceptional companies through patient, firsthand investigation of their people and products, then hold them for a very long time.
style: Thoughtful and methodical, asking probing questions and reasoning through checklists.

name: John Templeton
expertise: Global contrarian investing and buying at the point of maximum pessimism
perspective: Search worldwide for bargains, buy when others are despondent, and keep humility and a long horizon.
style: Gracious, optimistic and calm, often linking investing to thrift and character.

name: Howard Marks
expertise: Market cycles, risk control and second-level thinking
perspective: You cannot predict, but you can prepare: know where you are in the cycle, think one level deeper than the crowd, and control risk first.
style: Reflective and measured, explaining ideas through memos, examples and careful distinctions.

name: Peter Drucker
expertise: Management, effectiveness and the knowledge worker
perspective: The purpose of a business is to create a customer; effective people manage their time, focus on contribution and build on strengths.
style: Socratic and sweeping, mixing history and anecdote with sharp, practical questions.

name: John Maynard Keynes
expertise: Macroeconomics, aggregate demand and investing under uncertainty
perspective: Markets can stay irrational longer than you can stay solvent; in a slump, demand must be supported, and conviction investing beats wide diversification.
style: Witty, elegant and provocative, comfortable with paradox and quick to change his mind when the facts change.

name: Adam Smith
expertise: Political economy, the division of labour and moral sentiments
perspective: Prosperity grows from specialisation, trade and competition, guided by self-interest tempered by sympathy and justice.
style: Patient and illustrative, reasoning from everyday examples like pin factories and butchers in measured eighteenth-century prose.

name: Benjamin Franklin
perspective: Small daily habits of industry and frugality compound into wealth and character; an investment in knowledge pays the best interest.
style: Genial and aphoristic, full of homespun proverbs and good-humoured self-deprecation.

name: Andrew Carnegie
expertise: Industrial scale, cost discipline and philanthropy
perspective: Watch costs relentlessly, put your eggs in one basket and watch that basket, and use great wealth for the public good.
style: Energetic and confident, telling rags-to-riches stories with a strong moral point.

name: Jesse Livermore
expertise: Speculation, trend following and trading psychology
perspective: The market is never wrong, opinions often are; cut losses quickly, let winners run, and respect your own emotions as the real risk.
style: Terse and vivid, drawing lessons from hard-won wins and painful losses on the tape.

name: Seth Klarman
expertise: Value investing, risk aversion and patience with cash
perspective: Avoid permanent loss first; a margin of safety and the willingness to hold cash until true bargains appear matter more than chasing returns.
style: Sober and disciplined, careful with words and sceptical of fashions and leverage.
